pairs.evidence: apps/stage/src/fixture.test.ts:116 The test's name claims demo.jsonl is reproducible from its generator, but it only asserts that the first line is stream_start and the last is stream_end. A hand edit or a stale regeneration anywhere in the middle stays green.

techniques.evidence: apps/stage/src/fixture.test.ts:116 The name promises a stronger guard than its assertions make. Deleting or altering any interior line of the fixture leaves it green.

apps/stage/src/fixture.test.ts:117 The derived fixture names its generator, but its freshness is never checked against it (no regenerate-and-compare). Seeded-data honesty is otherwise good: every event type is covered (line 52), the ops are held to the segment tables' allowed_ops, and the demo case is checked as a byte copy (line 125).
apps/stage/src/live.test.ts:108 The live source's ack cadence, signal-lost slate and stall marks are driven by advanceTimersByTime rather than wall-clock waits.

apps/stage/src/App.tsx:345 The browser-automation probe is enabled by the runtime query flag ?debug=1 in the shipped bundle, not by a build-time switch. Compare App.tsx:232, where the face demo is gated by import.meta.env.DEV.

pairs.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-reconcile/src/tests_scale.rs:372 The ignored real-tournament measurement returns early, and so passes as ok, whenever load_source fails. The cause can be missing data or a corrupt one. A `cargo test -- --ignored` run reports the prompt-size budget as held when nothing was measured.

techniques.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-reconcile/src/tests_scale.rs:372 The test named weary_tournament_prompt_size can never reach its assertion yet still report green. It should skip loudly, or fail on a load error other than absence.
crates/shadowrunr-reconcile/src/tests_scale.rs:2 The 500-run scale cases use the cheapest fixture tier (in-memory synthetic runs). The hand-made t-fix fixture is read in place, never mutated.
crates/shadowrunr-reconcile/src/tests.rs:295 Each test that writes gets a private TempDir, which is discarded whole on drop, so tests inherit nothing from each other or from previous runs.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/e2e/resilience.rs:129 After the panic frame, the test waits a fixed 200 ms and then asserts the run slot was released by restarting it, which is a stopwatch-based ordering claim. Line 36 likewise sleeps 100 ms to assume the subscription is registered. On a loaded runner these go red with no defect present.

techniques.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/e2e/resilience.rs:129 The ordering (slot released before the restart) rests on a fixed sleep rather than an observed state or barrier. The 10 s and 60 s timeouts elsewhere (e.g. line 39) are proper loose, one-sided hang guards.
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/e2e/mod.rs:56 The checked-in sim fixture is copied byte-for-byte (no logic) into each test's tempdir. Tests mutate their private copy, and the copy is discarded whole.
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/e2e/mod.rs:90 Each e2e daemon binds port 0, with its own runs and data dirs in a tempdir. This virtualises the port singleton so the e2e tests can run in parallel.

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/tests/cli.rs:31 The CLI tests drive the actual built shadowrunr binary from outside, with a config in a tempdir. They read results back from the files it wrote rather than trusting the exit code alone.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: apps/stage/src/avatar/renderers.golden.test.ts:205 The renderers' recorded GL call streams are compared only as a truncated SHA-256 against constants. A failure gives no path to the first diverging call, and a re-baseline is a hash edit with no data diff to review. The prior stream is not stored; GOLDEN_DUMP writes only the current one.

techniques.evidence: apps/stage/src/avatar/renderers.golden.test.ts:205 This is a byte or hash comparison, not a structural one with a path. The snapshot's approval cannot be read in review. The record guard is right, though: the expected values are source constants (line 243), and GOLDEN_DUMP never rewrites them. This file is not in the context map's file list, but it guards this context's renderers.
apps/stage/src/avatar/driver.test.ts:20 Face motion is asserted over a deterministic stepped frame clock (1/60 s steps, seeded generator), never over wall time.
